key_insight: Chronicle is an explainable transformer that uses entire irregular treatment timelines to continuously update cancer risk predictions across many cancer types and outcomes.
clinical_relevance: It may help clinicians stratify patients more accurately, monitor risk over time, and support more individualized treatment planning across different hospital systems.
method: Trained on 53.7 million longitudinal data points from 51,711 patients with 67 cancer types
Learns directly from irregular timelines without imputation and jointly predicts eight clinical endpoints
Uses built-in explainability to link risk updates to patient-specific factors over time
evidence_signal: The model outperformed cross-sectional survival models (C-index 0.84 vs 0.76-0.79), predicted seven adverse-event/transfusion endpoints with AUC 0.80-0.92, and generalized to 69,341 patients across Germany, Switzerland, and the United States.
watch_item: Real-world deployment will need careful local validation and workflow integration because performance and calibration can vary across hospitals and patient populations.
paper_title: An explainable transformer model learning from entire treatment timelines for pan-cancer risk profiling across healthcare systems
